old_value: {"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-so3l","title":"Gateway first-boot provisioning has no recoverable transaction","description":"Security/robustness review finding: lichend commits the new identity seed first, then independently creates trust store, trust floor, slot replay store/floor, and finally RPL/OSCORE state. Any crash or I/O failure after save_seed leaves identity_created=false on the next boot, so the daemon takes the strict load path and permanently fails on whichever security artifact is missing/partial. Conversely the startup pre-existence guard runs only while identity_created=true and cannot resume. A transient first-boot failure therefore bricks the gateway until an operator manually decides which security files to delete, risking identity/state drift. Add a durable provisioning transaction/manifest with staged temp files and one atomic commit marker, or an idempotent resume path that verifies every existing artifact is bound to the persisted identity and never overwrites valid state; test interruption after every commit boundary.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"me@mark.atwood.name","created_at":"2026-08-24T16:43:41.358148Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-08-24T16:43:41.358148Z"}
